review_notes: I read the whole file and compared the parallel declarations. These were the left/right-limit lemmas, the two `vectorMeasure_bilinear_comp_eq` variants, the 12 Icc/Ioc/Ico/Ioo theorems, and the 12 scalar versions. I also checked Mathlib for an existing bilinear-tendsto lemma such as `Tendsto.clm_apply`. The grep found none under that name, so I couldn't confirm an existing API replacement. The primed `vectorMeasure_bilinear_comp_eq'` already reuses the unprimed one through symmetry. The `Icc`/`Ioc`/`Ico`/`Ioo` theorems are each a `rw` plus `simp`, and the scalar versions are direct wrappers, so I did not report them. `ext_of_Icc` and `setIntegral_Icc_rightLim_sub_leftLim_eq` have no duplicate proof elsewhere. The one genuine repetition is the pair of bilinear limit lemmas, and it is modest. The proposed helper has not been compiled, and the name `Tendsto.prodMk_nhds` is assumed from memory.

findings.problem: The two lemmas are line-for-line mirror copies with `𝓝[>]` swapped for `𝓝[<]` and `rightLim` for `leftLim`. The mathematical core is the same in both: if `f → a` and `g → b` along a filter, then `B (f x) (g x) → B a b`. It is proved by pairing the limits, rewriting with `nhds_prod_eq`, and composing with `B.continuous₂`. That core is written out twice, and any change to it (for example a different continuity argument) must be made in both places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a private lemma independent of any one-sided limit, for example:

private lemma tendsto_bilinear {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {u : ι → E} {v : ι → F} {a : E} {b : F} (B : E →L[ℝ] F →L[ℝ] G) (hu : Tendsto u l (𝓝 a)) (hv : Tendsto v l (𝓝 b)) : Tendsto (fun x ↦ B (u x) (v x)) l (𝓝 (B a b)) := (B.continuous₂.continuousAt (x := (a, b))).tendsto.comp (hu.prodMk_nhds hv)

The proof pairs the two limits and composes with continuity of `B` as a map on `E × F`. If Mathlib already has an equivalent lemma, use that instead.

Both uses then end with `exact tendsto_bilinear B (hf.tendsto_rightLim _) (hg.tendsto_rightLim _)` and the `leftLim` analogue. Each lemma then reads `ext x; rcases eq_or_neBot ... ; apply rightLim_eq_of_tendsto; exact tendsto_bilinear ...`. The hypotheses are unchanged: `hf`, `hg : BoundedVariationOn _ univ`, the same `E`, `F`, `G` instances, and `OrderTopology α`. The helper needs no extra imports.
findings.benefit: The continuity-of-pairing argument is stated and maintained once. Each of the two lemmas shrinks to its one-sided-limit case split plus a single application. The helper is also reusable for similar compositions with bilinear maps. The gain is modest, because the `NeBot` case split remains duplicated.
